It was a small moment early in the first period Saturday, around nine seconds before the Rangers scored their first goal in their win over the Kraken, but it captured an underlying factor in Mika Zibanejad’s start to the season.

In the Seattle zone, Zibanejad tried to pin defenseman Ryker Evans and jammed Evans’ stick into the air, causing enough havoc on the forecheck to force a long pass to the opposite corner — where Gabe Perreault collected possession. Two passes and one rebound later, Zibanejad, with a pair of Kraken defensemen closing in, sent a pass to Perreault, creating a goal that helped the Blueshirts take a lead just 95 seconds into the game.

The change of possession on the forecheck, leading to Zibanejad’s latest assist from near the corner, marked the latest example of how the 16-year veteran has changed his game.

“There’s no question” Zibanejad is playing with more physicality, head coach Mike Sullivan said last month.
news.content: پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. لحظه کوچکی در اوایل دوره اول شنبه بود، حدود 9 ثانیه قبل از اینکه رنجرز اولین گل خود را در پیروزی مقابل کراکن به ثمر رساند، اما این یک عامل اساسی در شروع فصل میکا زیبا نژاد بود. در منطقه سیاتل، زیبا نژاد سعی کرد رایکر ایوانز مدافع را سنجاق کند و چوب ایوانز را به هوا کوبید، و باعث خرابی کافی در جلوی چک شد تا یک پاس بلند به گوشه مقابل مجبور شود - جایی که گیب پررو مالکیت توپ را جمع کرد. دو پاس و یک ریباند بعد، زیبا نژاد در حالی که یک جفت مدافع کراکن در حال نزدیک شدن بود، یک پاس برای پررو فرستاد و گلی را خلق کرد که باعث شد آبی‌شاه‌ها تنها در 95 ثانیه از بازی پیش بیفتند. تغییر مالکیت توپ روی پیش‌چک، که منجر به آخرین پاس گل زیبای‌نژاد از نزدیکی کرنر شد، نشان‌دهنده آخرین نمونه از تغییر بازی این کهنه‌کار 16 ساله بود. مایک سالیوان سرمربی تیم ماه گذشته گفت: «شکی نیست» زیبا نژاد با آمادگی جسمانی بیشتری بازی می‌کند.

Brooklyn Heights has always had money. Now it has a velvet rope.

The landmarked neighborhood perched above the East River is getting the borough’s first branded condos, a members-only athletic club with a five-figure price tag and a buzzy chef-owned grocery. And it’s all while buyers are clawing over the few apartments that actually come up for sale.

“Since COVID, it has definitely taken on a completely different aura than it had pre-COVID,” Corcoran broker Deb Rieders told The Post. “It’s always been considered a great neighborhood. However, what’s happened since COVID … prices have exponentially gone up.”

The splashiest sign of the shift sits at 98 Montague St.

In September, Marriott International and developer SomeraRoad revealed plans to convert the 14-story Hotel Bossert, a 1909 Renaissance Revival landmark where the Brooklyn Dodgers toasted their 1955 World Series win, into the Ritz-Carlton Residences, Brooklyn Heights.

Owners will get a round-the-clock attended lobby, wellness and entertaining amenities and perks across Marriott’s global portfolio. Danny Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group will open its first full-service Brooklyn restaurant on the ground floor. Shovels are expected in the ground later this year, with a 2029 finish. Ryan Serhant’s firm is handling sales for units, whose prices are not yet available.

“We believe this project will become Brooklyn’s premier residential address and stand among the finest new residential offerings in New York City,” SomeraRoad founder Ian Ross said in a statement.

(If the luxury pitch sounds familiar, that’s because the Bossert has been here before. The Jehovah’s Witnesses sold the building to Joseph Chetrit of Chetrit Group and David Bistricer of Clipper Equity for $81 million in 2012, with plans for a boutique hotel. The reopening was pushed back again and again, and a planned fall 2017 debut under the name Esplendor Bossert never happened. Chetrit defaulted in May 2022 owing as much as $126.7 million, and a 2023 rescue attempt by hoteliers Ian Schrager and Ed Scheetz fizzled. Lender Beach Point Capital took the property at an uncontested foreclosure auction in February 2025, then sold it to SomeraRoad for $100 million that May.)

Rieders said the Ritz news caught the industry off guard, at first.

“I think it took all of us by surprise, though I’m not surprised at all, actually, given the bidding wars that I have on every single property that I have in the Heights,” she said.

“With wealthier residents comes a desire for fancier amenities.” Rieders said as for why a hotel brand would plant its flag there.

A few blocks away, Kings Athletic Club opened this fall in the base of the Hotel St. George co-op at 43 Clark St. The 52,000-square-foot playground packs two tennis courts, pickleball, a pool, squash courts, golf simulators, yoga and Pilates studios and a half basketball court. Red Hook Tavern founder Billy Durney runs the kitchen.

The club wouldn’t discuss pricing, but a source familiar with its options said annual memberships run between $30,000 and $70,000, and there’s already a waitlist.

The Ritz isn’t the only newcomer betting big on the neighborhood.

Landau Properties broke ground this summer on One Montague Place at 205 Montague St., a 50-story mixed-use tower that will deliver 46 condos, 90 rentals and 40,000 square feet of retail. Designed by Hill West Architects with interiors by Zarifi Design, the project is pitching a hotel-style lifestyle built around wellness, complete with a jazz club, a private membership club, and a lineup of leisure and entertainment spaces.

Pricing specifics are not yet available, but reports have indicated units will begin at roughly $6 million. Douglas Elliman’s Greg Williamson is the lead broker handling sales there.

“As someone born and raised in Brooklyn Heights who has represented numerous buildings in the area, I have never seen the neighborhood more desirable than it is today,” he told The Post. “We’re already seeing tremendous early interest and excitement surrounding the project.”

Rieders said the fiercest fights aren’t over the trophy townhouses. They’re over the relatively attainable apartments.

“Anything that’s in an ‘affordable’ price range goes into a bidding war,” she said. “Any co-ops or condos from one to four bedrooms, they all seem to go into bidding wars.”

Recent sales back her up. Take a two-bedroom at 89 State St. It hit the market at $1.67 million on Sept. 7, went into contract by Sept. 22 and closed Oct. 26 for $1.9 million, a cool $230,000 over ask.

Over at 75 Poplar St., another two-bedroom asking $1.65 million found a buyer within a week. It sold in September for $125,000 above the asking price.

The reason is basic supply and demand.

“There’s a serious lack of inventory,” Rieders said. “Almost every co-op and condo goes into a bidding war because people don’t really move. There’s not a tremendous amount of movement out, there’s just people who want to move in.”

“I would say in the $1 million to $5 million range, everything goes into a bidding war,” she added. One of her buyers “got outbid on about six things before they finally got an accepted offer.”

Neighborhood-wide, homes are going into contract in a median of 45 days, three days quicker than a year earlier, with a median sale price of about $1.77 million. At the very top, an off-market deal for a Civil War-era townhouse at 192 Columbia Heights closed for roughly $25 million, the priciest Brooklyn sale so far this year.

Rieders traces the frenzy to the pandemic, when Manhattanites wanted space and trees without straying far. They stayed for the schools, walkability and transit.

“It’s easier to commute from Brooklyn Heights than to almost any neighborhood in Manhattan because every single subway is there,” she said. And as a landmark district, “it’s very protected from development.”

Boldfacers caught on long ago. Matt Damon set a borough record with a $16.7 million penthouse at the Standish at 171 Columbia Heights, and Emily Blunt and John Krasinski followed with an $11 million full floor in the same building. Over the summer, Adam Driver shelled out $11.5 million for three units on the sixth floor of the building.

“I think regular people and celebrities are the same,” Rieders said. “So you feel like you live on Mayberry Lane, but you’re at the foot of the largest, most vibrant city in the world.”

The dining scene, long a weak spot, is catching up.

“It’s been a restaurant wasteland for years, quite frankly,” Rieders said. Now culinary-world darling Alison Roman is bringing a permanent Brooklyn Heights outpost of her boutique grocery and cafe, First Bloom, with speculation pointing to 144 Montague St.

And the money isn’t staying put. Rieders sees it spilling into neighboring enclaves like Cobble Hill, Boerum Hill and Carroll Gardens.

“It’s all the brownstone neighborhoods that are close to Manhattan,” she said.

“It feels like you live in a small town, but you have all of the benefit of living in the greatest city in the United States.”
news.content:

"این محله همیشه به عنوان یک محله عالی در نظر گرفته شده است. با این حال، آنچه از زمان کووید رخ داده است ... قیمت ها به طور تصاعدی افزایش یافته است."
شلوغ ترین علامت شیفت در خیابان مونتاگ 98 قرار دارد. در سپتامبر، Marriott International و توسعه‌دهنده SomeraRoad برنامه‌های خود را برای تبدیل هتل 14 طبقه Bossert، یک نقطه عطف احیای رنسانس در سال 1909، جایی که بروکلین داجرز برنده خود در سری جهانی 1955 را به نمایش گذاشتند، به اقامتگاه‌های Ritz-Carlton، Brooklyn Heights، نشان دادند. امکانات و مزایای سرگرم کننده در مجموعه جهانی ماریوت. گروه مهمان‌نوازی یونیون اسکوئر دنی مایر اولین رستوران بروکلین با خدمات کامل خود را در طبقه همکف افتتاح خواهد کرد. انتظار می‌رود که بیل‌ها در اواخر امسال و با پایان سال 2029 در زمین قرار گیرند. شرکت رایان سرهانت فروش واحدهایی را انجام می دهد که قیمت آنها هنوز در دسترس نیست. «ما معتقدیم که این پروژه به نشانی برتر مسکونی بروکلین تبدیل خواهد شد و در میان آنها قرار خواهد گرفت.

Wall Street’s whales are set to earn the fattest bonus haul in history, with the hottest trading desks expected to rake in massive 20% to 30% spikes in performance-related pay, according to a new report.

It’s not just the busiest desks that are poised to receive juicy paychecks. All the bonus-eligible employees at 15 major US and foreign banks will see bonus pools jump about 15% on average, according to a closely watched report released Tuesday by pay consultant Johnson Associates.

New York’s total bonus pool hit a record $49.2 billion last year, according to Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli, who also expects it to climb even higher.

Last year was good, “and this [year] is even better,” Alan Johnson, the firm’s managing director, told The Post.

“The whales in the ocean, of course, are the big banks for New York financials, and they did extremely well,” he added.

His firm dubbed 2026 the “year of the bank,” fueled by “record results in equity trading and underwriting.”

Johnson called the industry “very healthy, maybe euphoric.”

The biggest winners are stock traders and the bankers selling new shares, data compiled by Johnson Associates shows. They are expected to see whopping hikes of 20% to 30%

The survey also indicates that M&A advisers are in line for a 15% to 20% bonus boost; bank bosses, 10% to 20%; equities managers, 10% to 15%; and fixed-income traders, 7.5% to 12.5%.

The firm tracks bonus changes by percentages, leaving the raw multibillion-dollar tallies to government bean counters.

“If your business, the firm, is very successful, you’ll get paid really well,” Johnson said. “And if the firm and the business you’re attached to doesn’t do well, you won’t.”

He explained that many Wall Street titans are deciding to pay out bonuses to prevent top talent leaving for roles in private equity or the booming tech sector.

“Critical or excellent people are worth more, and you don’t need as many of them,” Johnson said. “But average people are worth less and replaceable.

“As always, you’ve got competition from other banks. You’ve got competition from private markets, he added. “You certainly have competition from AI and others.”

AI has also been driving job cuts on Wall Street, according to reports, with bots increasingly handling the heavy lifting that once required armies of young analysts — from building pitch books to checking strict compliance rules. That lets firms slash mid-level payrolls and hoard the cash.

“I think certainly, as you look at trading, for example, you’re going to have fewer associates, analysts, vice presidents. I think that’s happening. I think technology is replacing people,” Johnson said.

AI appears to be impacting Goldman Sachs’ payroll — the bank’s pay bill surged 17% to $16.6 billion in the first nine months of the year, even as its overall staff shrank by 2%.

In a recent CNBC interview, Goldman President and COO John Waldron noted that AI allows the bank to grow its output without a massive hiring spree.

“We can actually scale the firm, be more valuable to our clients,” he said. “I think a lot of enterprises are starting to see that”.

Wall Street titans are also throwing exclusive titles and cold hard cash at their top dealmakers to fend off private equity poachers.

The buyout barons remain a constant threat, luring away prime banking talent with the promise of highly lucrative profit-sharing deals.

Goldman appears to have deployed this defensive playbook. The banking giant elevated a massive 109 employees to its elite partner ranks last week, the largest class since 2010.

The Wall Street giant also named a record 13 engineers as partners, proving that one of the hottest bidding wars on the Street is now for the nerds.

Johnson said private equity is still a threat to banking talent but has been “supplemented by the pull of AI firms.”

His bullish forecast for New York’s financial sector marked a stark contrast to the gloomy outlook earlier this year from City Hall, which predicted a bust.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s May budget had Wall Street profits hitting $45 billion this year, down from a record $65 billion in total profits last year.

The Street blew past the $45 billion mark in just six months, with DiNapoli saying profits could top $90 billion if the pace holds.

Still, top compensation expert Johnson warned Wall Street bankers that the champagne may run dry by next New Year’s Eve.

His study expects “2026 to mark a peak against a potentially weaker 2027,” citing geopolitical turmoil, rising inflation and a possible AI “bubble” looming over the market.

“You rarely see everything being good at the same time,” Johnson added.

پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. نهنگ های وال استریت قرار است چاق ترین پاداش تاریخ را به دست آورند، با توجه به گزارش جدید، انتظار می رود داغ ترین میزهای معاملاتی 20 تا 30 درصد در پرداخت های مرتبط با عملکرد افزایش پیدا کنند. این فقط شلوغ ترین میزها نیستند که آماده دریافت دستمزد آبدار هستند. طبق گزارشی که روز سه‌شنبه توسط مشاور حقوقی جانسون آسوشیتز منتشر شد، تمامی کارکنان واجد شرایط دریافت پاداش در 15 بانک بزرگ ایالات متحده و خارجی به طور متوسط ​​شاهد افزایش حدود 15 درصدی پاداش‌ها خواهند بود. طبق گزارش توماس دی ناپولی، که همچنین پیش‌بینی می‌کند که حتی بالاتر از این نیز باشد، مجموع پاداش‌های نیویورک در سال گذشته به رکورد 49.2 میلیارد دلار رسید. آلن جانسون، مدیر عامل شرکت، به روزنامه پست گفت: «سال گذشته خوب بود، «و امسال [سال] حتی بهتر است.» او افزود: «البته نهنگ‌های اقیانوس بانک‌های بزرگی برای امور مالی نیویورک هستند و بسیار خوب عمل کردند».
جانسون این صنعت را "بسیار سالم، شاید سرخوش" نامید. داده‌های جمع‌آوری‌شده توسط Johnson Associates نشان می‌دهد که بزرگترین برندگان معامله‌گران سهام و بانکدارانی هستند که سهام جدید می‌فروشند. انتظار می رود که آنها شاهد افزایش چشمگیر 20 تا 30 درصدی باشند.
این نظرسنجی همچنین نشان می‌دهد که مشاوران M&A در صف افزایش پاداش 15 تا 20 درصدی هستند. روسای بانک، 10 تا 20 درصد؛ مدیران سهام، 10 تا 15 درصد؛ و معامله گران با درآمد ثابت، 7.5٪ تا 12.5٪. شرکت تغییرات پاداش را بر اساس درصد دنبال می کند.

Foreign “honeytrap” spies are a serious blind spot in the US’s national security defenses — as the case of Jensen Huang highlights.

The Nvidia CEO admitted an affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang (no relation) this weekend — who is also suspected of manipulating her mark to get banned high-powered processing chips into her home country for the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

His case is not an anomaly, as spies from Russia, Iran, North Korea and especially China find infiltrating the US and either getting elected to positions of responsibility or seducing those in power one of the best ways to extract data or influence policy.

China’s Ministry of State Security comes from a tradition which “celebrates getting inside the adversary’s decision making and shaping what they do,” Peter Mattis, a former CIA counterintelligence analyst and president of the Jamestown Foundation, told The Post.

“Intelligence is not about the collection of classified information. Intelligence is about supporting decisions, supporting decision makers and policymakers.”

In today’s climate, there is no business more cutting edge and competitive and AI, which is why computer geeks in all positions at tech companies everywhere are constantly being warned to be on the lookout.

Or, as Elon Musk once pointed out in a cheeky reply to a story about so-called sex warfare waged by rogue nations, “If she’s a 10, you’re an asset.”

The same applies in politics. Ex-California congressman Eric Swalwell had a strong campaign to become the next governor of the state until it emerged he’d had a sexual relationship with suspected Chinese spy Christine Fang, known as “Fang Fang,” who had infiltrated his office while under FBI surveillance, it emerged earlier this year.

Once Fang realized she was being watched she fled back to China. She had originally come to the US on a student visa and has been accused of seducing two mayors in the Midwest — whose names have never been revealed —before Swalwell, FBI reports claimed.

It was later determined Swalwell, who was also accused of sexual harassment by other women, had broken no laws in his relationship with Fang.

Not all alleged infiltrations are sexual. Linda Sun, a former Aide to New York Governors Andrew Cuomo and Kathy Hochul was put on trial for allegedly using her official state position to advance Beijing’s interests, such as blocking Taiwanese officials from leadership and forging signatures. Her case ended in a mistrial.

Meanwhile, the mayor of Arcadia in California, Eileen Wang, 56, stepped down from her position days before being charged with acting as an illegal agent of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) in May. She has yet to face trial.

Mattis warned that not everyone starts out as a spy, and in many cases foreign governments seek to exploit relationships which have already been established.

In the case of Huang — who worked for tech firms which imported Nvidia chips, but not to China — the precise sequence is yet to be determined.

“It’s not clear whether they saw the relationship [Jensen and Alice] and then tried to exploit it,” Mattis said.

An alternative, he said, was Chinese intelligence already having a relationship with Alice Huang and seeking to exploit her business contacts.

“If you trust someone, you talk to them about things that you might not talk about with other people,” Mattis said.

Shared professional interests can also make probing questions about supply, customers and policy sound perfectly ordinary.

Mattis said foreign nations are interested in supply chains and commercial pressure points — but also shaping what their honeytraps tell others in power.

“The mission would be to exploit someone who can shape an executive’s view of things so that they will make particular recommendations,” he said.

The scale of operations is very hard to gauge.

In January 2022, then-FBI director Christopher Wray said more than 2,000 investigations concerned Chinese government efforts to steal American information or technology.

The bureau was opening a new China-related counterintelligence case roughly every 12 hours. Those figures counted investigations, not individual spies or honeytraps.

Mattis described China’s Ministry of State Security as a “vast sprawling apparatus,” encompassing the central ministry, 34 provincial departments and bureaus, and hundreds of local offices.

He estimated its overall workforce could reach “600,000, 700,000” officers, but stressed they most focus on activity inside China.

Partly for this reason and because of suspicions over honeytrapping, the Biden administration prevented any US government officials in China from having sex with Chinese women. Trump has continued the same prohibition.

Still, operations outside of the mainland from China and Russia range from the most sophisticated to the quite brazen.

“I’m getting an enormous number of very sophisticated LinkedIn requests from the same type of attractive young Chinese woman,” James Mulvenon, chief intelligence officer at risk-assessment firm Pamir Consulting, noted to The Times last year.

Many suspected spies are willing to be deep undercover and play the long game too.

“Showing up, marrying a target, having kids with a target — and conducting a lifelong collection operation, it’s very uncomfortable to think about but it’s so prevalent,” one former counterespionage official noted in the same report.

Having used this model but been busted, ten Russian agents pleaded guilty in 2010 to conspiring to operate unlawfully in the US. Some used stolen identities while building ordinary-looking lives and relationships, according to the FBI.

Russian national Maria Butina later admitted conspiring to act as an agent of Russia after cultivating politically influential Americans and organizations to establish unofficial communication channels. She was sentenced to 18 months in 2019.

Foreign adversaries often infiltrate and exploit communities already in the US as the first step into the US.

“A key way they will conduct espionage is through Chinese-American communities and groups which are sympathetic to the state … this is just the start. Stealing trade secrets and academic research are all part of the Chinese playbook.

“It is a whole party effort by the CCP to undermine the American way of life and threaten American innovation and dominance,” Andrew Harding of The Heritage Foundation recently told The Post.

For example, Chinese intelligence officer, Yanjun Xu, helped lure a GE Aviation employee into delivering a presentation at a Chinese university as part of an effort to obtain aviation trade secrets. Xu was convicted and sentenced in 2022. He was later pardoned Biden.

Most worryingly, those who do not comply or their families can be threatened, even if they abscond from their duties.

Mattis said Chinese authorities do not hesitate to exploit genuine relationships by threatening a partner or their family.

“They’ll say: ‘We’ll harm this person and their family if you don’t cooperate with us’,” he added.

news.originalContent:
The French government said it is seeking tough sanctions to deter further cyberattacks across Europe.

France says it has summoned Iran’s ambassador to Paris “to lodge a very strong protest” after it accused Tehran of carrying out a major cyberattack targeting supermarket fridges last month.

“It marks the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation’s interests and the security of the French people,” Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday.

“I can also tell you that we rule nothing out and will take all measures – including those we may not disclose publicly – that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks,” he added.

Barrot, speaking on France Info ‌‌television, said the government would push for European Union sanctions in response to what he called an “attack of unprecedented scale and aggression in our country”.

He said firm measures would be taken “to deter anyone who might be tempted, in Iran or elsewhere, to do it again”.

On Monday, Barrot said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was behind cyberattacks targeting more than 700 French supermarkets on October 11 and 12, when refrigerators were remotely accessed “to initiate abnormal, indefinite defrost cycles”.

Raised temperatures in fridges forced the supermarkets to throw away all perishable food.

Millions of euros’ worth of food was spoiled, according to retailers. In some cases, the raised temperatures sparked fires or melted equipment.

French supermarket groups E-Leclerc, Intermarche, Carrefour, Monoprix and Cooperative U were all hit.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said on Monday she had opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit of the IRGC, over the attacks.

The prosecutor’s office has requested international arrest warrants be issued for two Shahid Kaveh officials.

Similar incidents have since been reported in other European countries.

In a suspected cyberattack on November 2, temperature spikes were recorded in stores in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden.

Jody Westby, chief executive of Global Cyber Risk LLC, said tracking down the group directly responsible for the attacks is “very difficult” because of poor cooperation on international cybercrime investigations.

“It’s been a problem for 20 some years, and now it’s a little better, but only marginally so,” Westby told Al Jazeera. She said that it was difficult to track and trace the origin of such attacks “because of the nature of packet switching”.

In recent days, European air traffic has also been disrupted by false bomb alerts against dozens of flights, although the origin of those threats has yet to be determined.
news.content: دولت فرانسه گفت که به دنبال تحریم‌های سخت‌گیرانه برای جلوگیری از حملات سایبری بیشتر در سراسر اروپا است. فرانسه می‌گوید پس از متهم کردن تهران به انجام یک حمله سایبری بزرگ که در ماه گذشته یخچال‌های سوپرمارکت‌ها را هدف قرار داده بود، سفیر ایران در پاریس را احضار کرده است تا «اعتراض بسیار شدیدی ارائه کند». ژان نوئل بارو، وزیر امور خارجه فرانسه، روز سه‌شنبه گفت: «این اولین حمله سایبری در مقیاس بزرگ با هدف خرابکاری در قلمرو ملی ما است و یک حمله بزرگ به منافع کشور و امنیت مردم فرانسه است.» «همچنین می‌توانم به شما بگویم که ما هیچ چیز را منتفی نمی‌کنیم و همه اقدامات را انجام خواهیم داد - از جمله اقداماتی که ممکن است به طور علنی فاش نکنیم. بارو که در تلویزیون فرانس اینفو صحبت می‌کرد، گفت که دولت در واکنش به آنچه «حمله‌ای در مقیاس بی‌سابقه و تجاوز به کشور ما» خواند، تحریم‌های اتحادیه اروپا را اعمال خواهد کرد. بارو روز دوشنبه گفت که سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی ایران پشت حملات سایبری بود که بیش از 700 سوپرمارکت فرانسوی را در 11 و 12 اکتبر هدف قرار دادند، زمانی که یخچال‌ها از راه دور «برای شروع چرخه‌های یخ‌زدایی غیرعادی و نامحدود» دسترسی داشتند. به گفته خرده فروشان خراب شده است. در برخی موارد، مطرح شده است

On her first day in office, Texas Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa plans to freeze residential electricity rates in response to what she described as an affordability crisis.

“On Day One as governor, I’ll freeze residential electricity rates and make corporations finally pay their fair share,” Hinojosa said in an interview with a local energy data group.

She reiterated the plan in an interview with the Texas Tribune, stating, “Within an hour of taking the oath of office, I will declare a high-cost emergency in the state of Texas and issue an emergency executive order to … freeze electricity rates.”

The plan is raising concerns that such a freeze will clash with Texas’ uniquely competitive energy sector, which relies heavily on free-market choice, and that it could inadvertently create energy shortages as suppliers are prevented from adjusting their prices.

That’s the concern of Nick Loris, the president of C3 Solutions, a conservative coalition for climate solutions that focuses on energy, environment and agriculture policy.

He expects the emergency declaration will face legal challenges almost immediately from energy providers. In particular, he cast doubt on the scope of the emergency declaration.

“The Texas Disaster Act lets the governor declare disasters and suspend the regulatory laws and statutes that are in existence. But I think there is a high degree of skepticism, both from courts but also from state policymakers, that this warrants such a claim — and that it is such a disaster,” Loris told Fox News Digital.

“I would imagine if there were legal challenges, it would come from those affected parties,” he added.

Loris explained that Texas has fostered one of the most competitive energy environments in the country.

In 1999, the state passed Senate Bill 7 — a piece of legislation that opened most of the state to retail choice, allowing customer to pick their preferred retail electric providers (REPs), beginning in 2002.

“The legislature finds that the production and sale of electricity is not a monopoly warranting regulation of rates, operations, and services and that the public interest in competitive electric markets requires that, except for transmission and distribution services and for the recovery of stranded costs, electric services and their prices should be determined by customer choices and the normal forces of competition,” the Texas Legislature wrote in the law.

As a result of the law, Texas largely operates its own independent energy grid and runs an energy-only wholesale market in which generators are paid primarily for the electricity they produce rather than for standing capacity.

Texas has over 100 REPs that energy consumers can pick from, each competing for consumers’ business.

To Loris, the range of choices provides a remarkable amount of flexibility for consumers.

“It’s like shopping at a grocery store for cereal for your retail electricity. There’s so much choice that you can enter into. Short-term contracts, long-term contracts, use different fuel sources,” Loris said.

However, he warned that a utilitiesrfreeze undermines that competitive environment, causing providers to shoulder the burden of fluctuating supply.

“If the electricity suppliers are not covering the costs that they incur, that’s going to leave them worse off and make it more vulnerable for them to adequately provide that power,” Loris said.

“Price signals really kind of act like a traffic light. They tell people when to speed up, when to slow down, or when to come to a full stop,” he added.

Having won her Nov. 3 gubernatorial race, Hinojosa will be sworn in on Jan. 19, 2027.

Her office did not immediately respond to requests for comment on what her response would be if the rate freezes resulted in an energy shortage.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Lame-duck House Speaker Mike Johnson blasted voters for making the “wrong choice” in this month’s midterms — while also predicting a circus will run wild on Capitol Hill during President Trump’s final two years in office.

Johnson, who will lose the speakership when the Democrats take up the majority in the 120th Congress in January, hailed the first two years of the second Trump administration and dismissed suggestions the commander-in-chief should change course following the GOP’s shellacking that saw the party lose control of both chambers of Congress.

“I’m not going to tell the president how to do his job, we have an incredible record,” Johnson, who has ruled himself out of the race to be the GOP’s Minority Leader in the next Congress, told CNN Sunday – less than a week after the Democrats flipped more than 40 House seats.

“I’m sorry that the voters made the wrong choice. I really do believe that the next two years is going to be a bit of a circus. It’s going to be chaos… and that’s a great tragedy.

“If we had kept the majority, we would stay on course to continue delivering for the people and I just don’t know how that’s going to work [going] forward.”

Johnson is the most senior Republican who has lashed out at voters for making the so-called “wrong choice” at the ballot box.

A postmortem into the GOP’s shellacking is underway, with Vice President JD Vance blaming the bloodbath on the Iran war, while President Trump alluded to how the conflict drove up gasoline prices.

Instead of scolding voters, outgoing Florida governor Ron DeSantis blamed “corporatist Republicans” for young Americans having a negative perception of capitalism and leading towards socialism.

Meanwhile, buoyant Democrats have already vowed to use their newfound subpoena power to investigate members of the Trump inner circle as well as administration officials following last Tuesday’s blowout victory.

Pete Hegseth, the Secretary of War, is facing impeachment – either in the lame-duck session of Congress or when Democrats take up the majority.

Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), who is poised to take the speaker’s gavel in the new year, has already vowed he is a “hard yes” on impeaching Hegseth, claiming the Secretary of War has “abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.”

Democrats are set to meet Tuesday to discuss the resolution – which is being spearheaded by lame-duck congressman Thomas Massie (R-Ky.).

Mike Johnson: “I’m sorry that the voters made the wrong choice. I really do believe that this next two years is going to be a bit of a circus. It’s going to be chaos …. and that’s a great tragedy.” pic.twitter.com/HacOAzwXjN

Johnson, meanwhile, believes it would be a foolish move to impeach Hegseth amid the conflict with Iran.

“Impeaching a cabinet secretary right now, especially the Department of War in the middle of hostilities abroad, would be a terrible look,” he told CNN.

“We don’t impeach cabinet secretaries for political gain or cheap tricks and I think everybody knows that’s what that is.”

The last cabinet secretary to be impeached was Alejandro Mayorkas, the Secretary of Homeland Security, in February 2024.

He was accused of a willful and systematic refusal to comply with immigration laws and a breach of public trust.

His impeachment never went to trial in the Senate – with the upper chamber dismissing the charges as unconstitutional.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington renews its push to end the war that followed Moscow’s all-out invasion nearly five years ago.

The two-day session in the UAE’s capital, Abu Dhabi, is the first such meeting since February.

It will focus on security guarantees, the White House said before the discussions.

Russia sees NATO as a threat, and Ukraine wants to prevent future Russian invasions.

Hopes of progress in ending Europe’s biggest conflict since World War II are tempered by the absence of any significant breakthroughs in three previous rounds of talks early this year.

The war has already killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians, analysts and humanitarian organizations say.

There are no signs the fighting is abating, and the talks took place against a backdrop of new long-range strikes between Russia and Ukraine. The two armies are largely deadlocked on the front line.

Russia launched 162 drones of various types and a ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight, Ukraine’s air force said.

Meanwhile, Russia’s Ministry of Defense said that its forces shot down 155 Ukrainian drones overnight above eight Russian regions, as well as the Crimean Peninsula, which Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014.

US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a “negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment.”

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, noted at the start of the talks that the Russian delegation “has become bigger and more professional.”

He expressed hope that the meeting “will allow us to advance on the path towards peace in the interests of the people of Russia and the people of Ukraine.”

Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service who is leading Kyiv’s delegation, said that the day began with a meeting between the Ukrainian team, the US envoys and representatives from the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission.

The Russian and Ukrainian governments remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal.

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.

Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won’t agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that it would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles.

He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was visiting Denmark on Tuesday, rejects Putin’s demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia hasn’t been able to take on the battlefield.

Zelensky also rejects any limits on Ukraine’s military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelensky is the only way territorial issues can be settled.

The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.

Russia’s chief negotiator is Medinsky, a Putin aide who has led Moscow’s team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff’s operational department, Yuri Zhigarlovsky.

Apart from Umerov, the Ukrainian delegation also reportedly includes Zelensky’s chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy, Sergiy Kyslytsya, and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Zelensky’s Servant of the People party.

Last week, Trump declared that some kind of grand deal about European security was in the works, describing it as “a big agreement” that is “going to involve more than Ukraine.”

Kushner said Monday on X that a “comprehensive and lasting settlement will also require direct engagement between Russia and our European partners on the broader security arrangements that affect them.” The discussions in Abu Dhabi will set the stage for “that engagement to begin in the near future, as part of a broader multilateral process,” he said.

Moscow has praised the broad approach.

“We can only welcome the (U.S.) negotiators on President Donald Trump’s request proposing to put the issue of collective security on top of the agenda of the talks on a Ukrainian settlement,” Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said.

Just before Moscow launched the full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, it demanded that NATO roll back its deployments in the trans-Atlantic alliance’s member countries in Central and Eastern Europe, seeing their presence as a security threat. Similar demands will likely be part of any comprehensive peace deal proposed by Russia.

Kushner said that before the start of the three-way talks, he and Witkoff would meet separately with envoys from Ukraine, the European Union, NATO, Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Italy to “continue the close consultation and coordination we have undertaken on European security and Ukraine’s postwar future over the past several weeks.”

Some in the EU see Washington’s proposals as too accommodating to Moscow.

Russia has objected to the Europeans’ involvement in the three-way talks, but said that EU representatives could join at a later stage.

While the ground battles have morphed into a war of attrition along the about 750-mile front line, Russia and Ukraine have ramped up their long-range strikes with drones and missiles.

Russia has intensified its air campaign against Ukraine’s power grid, seeking to weaken the country’s resolve as winter sets in. Moscow has relied on ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, taking advantage of Ukraine’s shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has escalated its drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر مشاهده کنید. گفتگوهای سه جانبه بین روسیه، اوکراین و ایالات متحده از روز سه شنبه در امارات متحده عربی آغاز شد، زیرا واشنگتن تلاش خود را برای پایان دادن به جنگی که پس از حمله همه جانبه مسکو تقریباً پنج سال پیش به دنبال داشت، تجدید می کند. جلسه دو روزه در ابوظبی، پایتخت امارات متحده عربی، اولین نشست از این قبیل از ماه فوریه است. گفته می شود که کاخ سفید بر روی امنیت تمرکز خواهد کرد. روسیه ناتو را به عنوان یک تهدید می‌بیند و اوکراین می‌خواهد از تهاجمات روسیه در آینده جلوگیری کند. تحلیلگران و سازمان‌های بشردوستانه می‌گویند که امید به پیشرفت در پایان دادن به بزرگترین درگیری اروپا از زمان جنگ جهانی دوم به دلیل نبود هیچ پیشرفت مهمی در سه دور قبلی مذاکرات در اوایل سال جاری کاهش یافته است. هیچ نشانه ای مبنی بر کاهش درگیری وجود ندارد و گفتگوها در پس زمینه حملات دوربرد جدید بین روسیه و اوکراین انجام شد. دو ارتش تا حد زیادی در خط مقدم به بن‌بست رسیده‌اند. نیروی هوایی اوکراین گفت که روسیه 162 پهپاد از انواع مختلف و یک موشک بالستیک را در طول شب به سمت اوکراین پرتاب کرد. در همین حال، وزارت دفاع روسیه گفت که نیروهای این کشور 155 پهپاد اوکراینی را در طول شب در بالای هشت منطقه روسیه و همچنین شبه جزیره کریمه را که روسیه در سال 2014 از اوکراین ضمیمه کرد، سرنگون کرد. داماد دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا، جرد کوشنر، در X گفت که او و استیو ویتکاف، فرستاده همکارش در حال کار بر روی یک پروژه هستند.

news.originalContent:
ردیاب‌های پرواز نشان می‌دهند که حداقل ۹ هواپیمای سوخت‌رسان نظامی آمریکا یک پایگاه هوایی در شرق انگلستان را ترک کرده‌اند.

وال استریت جورنال گزارش می‌دهد که هواپیماها در پاسخ به تهدید ایران از پایگاه نیروی هوایی سلطنتی میلدنهال منتقل شده‌اند.

ارتش آمریکا یا وزارت دفاع بریتانیا هنوز این موضوع را تایید نکرده‌اند.

به گزارش وال استریت جورنال، چندین هواپیمای نظامی ایالات متحده روز دوشنبه، ۹ نوامبر، یک پایگاه هوایی دیگر در بریتانیا را ترک کرده‌اند.

گزارش وال استریت جورنال می‌گوید که دو هواپیمای سوخت‌رسان آمریکا که از پایگاه نیروی هوایی سلطنتی میلدنهال در سافک استفاده می‌کردند، اوایل روز دوشنبه به آلمان تغییر مسیر دادند. بعد در همان روز چندین هواپیمای سوخت‌رسان دیگر در این پایگاه به آلمان و دیگر جاها منتقل شدند.

این روزنامه به نقل از مقامات آمریکایی گزارش داد که این اقدام در پاسخ به تهدید ایران انجام شده است.

این اقدام چند هفته پس از آن صورت می‌گیرد که ایالات متحده بمب‌افکن‌های خود را از پایگاه نیروی هوایی سلطنتی فرفورد به‌دلیل یک حادثه امنیتی مشکوک خارج کرد. دولت بریتانیا این حادثه امنیتی را «به احتمال زیاد» مرتبط با ایران دانست اما ایران این را تکذیب کرده است.

لوسی پاول، وزیر آموزش بریتانیا، در پاسخ به سوالی در مورد رفتن هواپیماهای آمریکایی از پایگاه نیروی هوایی سلطنتی میلدنهال، به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «بدیهی است که نمی‌توانم در مورد مسائل عملیاتی جاری اظهار نظر کنم اما به شما اطمینان می‌دهم که ما امنیت و ایمنی پایگاه‌های خود را فوق‌العاده جدی می‌گیریم و همیشه در صورت نیاز بر اساس اطلاعات امنیتی اقدام خواهیم کرد.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

سخنگوی وزارت دفاع بریتانیا هم به بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «این روال نیست که درمورد فعالیت‌های کشورهای دیگر اظهار نظر کنیم. هواپیماها و سایر دارایی‌ها طبق الزامات عملیاتی منظم جابجا می‌شوند.»

لرد ریکتس، مشاور سابق امنیت ملی بریتانیا، هم به برنامه رادیویی «تودی» بی‌بی‌سی گفت: «ما درمورد یک پایگاه هوایی صحبت می‌کنیم که هواپیماهای سوخت‌رسان بزرگ را در خود جای داده است. البته که آنها اهداف بزرگی هستند؛ یک پایگاه هوایی محیطی وسیع و بزرگ دارد و لاجرم آسیب‌پذیر است.»

لرد ریکتس افزود: «در این مرحله هیچ‌کس نمی‌داند این اطلاعات چه بوده است. من گمان می‌کنم بخشی از آن از روی احتیاط زیاد است.»

این تحولات در پایگاه نیروی هوایی سلطنتی میلدنهال پس از یک حادثه امنیتی در پایگاه نیروی هوایی سلطنتی فرفورد، پایگاه نیروی هوایی ایالات متحده در گلاسترشر، رخ می‌دهد.

در ماه سپتامبر، پس از مشاهده سه ون مشکوک در نزدیکی آن پایگاه، اعلام شد که حادثه امنیتی بزرگی روی داده است. بعدتر مشخص شد که ایالات متحده بمب‌افکن‌های خود را از پایگاه خارج کرده و به آمریکا بازگردانده است.

دو تبعه بریتانیا در ارتباط با این حادثه در دادگاه حاضر شدند.

news.originalContent:
Harrison, 81, becomes the oldest winner of the prestigious prize, whose previous winners include Salman Rushdie and Margaret Atwood.

British ‌‌author M John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize ⁠⁠for his ⁠⁠dystopian satire novel, The End of Everything, becoming ⁠⁠the oldest winner in the literary award’s history.

The Booker judges unanimously selected the 198-page book on Monday, saying it can be read as a “thriller, a mystery, a satire, a dystopia, a road novel, a work of realism”.

The novel, whose themes of “catastrophe and apocalypse” chime with our uneasy times, is the first work of science fiction to win the prestigious literary award.

Harrison beat five other finalists, including previous winners Douglas Stuart and Marlon James. He was awarded the 50,000 British pound ($67,000) prize at a ceremony in London.

The End of Everything is set on the southeast English coast in the near future, after an unspecified calamity shattered society and brought an influx of enigmatic alien entities to Britain. It centres on a beachcomber who lives with his gun-toting aunt and discovers a puzzling, shape-shifting artefact on the shore.

“It’s a grim world, and it’ll keep on being grim. And it’s weird. But at the end of things, there may be some kind of – I wouldn’t say hope, or closure, but there might be some kind of relief,” Harrison said, when asked what he wanted to convey to readers.

The 81-year-old author is the oldest writer to win the Booker, two years older than Margaret Atwood when she won in 2019.

Previous winners also include Salman Rushdie, Ian McEwan and Arundhati Roy. Last year’s winner was Flesh by Hungarian-British writer David Szalay.

Critics have praised the book’s dark humour, though some have been confused by its elusive narrative.

Mary Beard, who chaired the judging panel, described the book as “the politics of now seen through the lens of the future”, saying it depicts a society grappling with ⁠⁠a catastrophe its inhabitants do not fully understand.

“What he does is to say, when the catastrophe comes, you won’t know what’s happening,” the historian said. “And there are bits where you, the reader, are with the characters in not fully understanding. Now, I think that’s fantastically exciting.”

Harrison’s win marks a rare moment of mainstream recognition for the science fiction genre. He previously said he had been “working for 40 to 50 years to shift the balance, both as a novelist and as a critic. Why shouldn’t a well-written [work of science fiction] be considered to be literary fiction?”

Beard said Harrison’s win was “recognition of what some people would see as the blindingly obvious, that you find great books in every genre.”

Founded in 1969, the Booker Prize is open to English-language novels from any country published in the UK and Ireland and has a reputation for transforming writers’ careers.

If its other failings weren’t maddening enough, now the $45 billion city Department of Education is  hiring obvious psychos to work with kids and paying “principals” $200,000 to run nonexistent schools.

Sayed Mohassib allegedly slaughtered jogger Katie Suarez near the Belt Parkway in Bath Beach Oct. 30; he claims he found himself sitting on a nearby bench, drenched in blood but with no knowledge of why.

Scariest of all, he was then working as a substitute paraprofessional at PS 200, a position of trust and responsibility helping young children.

Did anyone check his background? After a red-flag few weeks with the NYPD, he joined the Marines only to get discharged on psychiatric grounds, then be rejected for reinstatement as a cop — and that very same day win transport to Bellevue because of his erratic behavior.

In 2024, cops took him to Coney Island Hospital after he threatened to “chop” his mother and sister into pieces.

Despite extensive documentation of Mohassib’s instability, the DOE somehow hired him as a substitute paraprofessional, a low-paid though hands-on position that typically requires personal nomination by the school principal.

Meanwhile, Caleb Haraguchi-Combs is earning close to $200,000 a year to serve as principal of an AI/fintech high school . . . which doesn’t exist.

Higherups’ decision to abort that school didn’t trouble Manhattan High School Superintendent Gary Beidleman enough to bump Haraguchi-Combs back to his prior salary or otherwise find him a school to run.

Meanwhile, schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels is neck-deep in accounting and contracting scandals related to his approval of lucrative no-bid contracts, as well his refusal to release information on more than $10 billion in third-party expenditures.

And none of this touches the real outrage: most DOE schools’ failure to teach kids how to read, write and do simple math, even as enrollment continues to plummet as any parents who can gets their kids out of the system.

It seems the system is now designed to produce nothing but scandal.

news.originalContent:
The ousted leader faces the prospect of being hanged upon return for her violent suppression of the 2024 uprising that killed more than 1,400 people.

Dhaka, Bangladesh – Bangladesh’s ousted leader Sheikh Hasina wants a new passport to return to the country next month, more than two years after fleeing to India following a mass uprising that forced her from power.

The 79-year-old former prime minister was sentenced to death in absentia last year for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on the student-led protests in 2024, a charge she denies.

She faces the prospect of being hanged upon her return, as the government that succeeded her remains a staunch political opponent.

Dhaka has already rejected the passport request and has challenged Hasina to seek extradition from India if she is serious about returning home.

“Bangladesh does not give passports to terrorists who kill thousands of people and flee. It will work under the current extradition arrangements with India to pursue and get the terrorist Hasina handed over,” State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir told Al Jazeera.

On Tuesday, the Bangladeshi prosecutor Md Aminul Islam, who secured the death sentence for Hasina at the Dhaka-based International Crimes Tribunal, said she will be executed if she returns home.

“Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,” Islam told reporters.

So, what led Hasina to approach the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, seeking a new passport and a national identity card since her existing documents have been revoked, and what is her game plan?

Hasina ruled Bangladesh with an iron fist for nearly 20 years and still enjoys support among a section of its population, while many others want to see her hanged.

Her return could worsen political tensions as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government tries to restore ‌‌stability two years on from the 2024 uprising that led to the killing of more than 1,400 people, according to the United Nations.

But analysts question whether Hasina genuinely intends to return to face the law, or is using the promise to revive her political fortunes from self-imposed exile in India.

For Zillur Rahman, president of the Centre for Governance Studies, a Dhaka-based think tank, Hasina’s passport request is less about an imminent plan to return and more about keeping herself politically relevant as she tries to retain control of her Awami League party.

“I think she knows what her fate is. But what she wants is to keep Awami League leaders and activists politically engaged,” he said, referring to Hasina’s party, which was founded by her father and Bangladesh independence movement leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

“As far as I understand, she does not want to hand over the party’s leadership to anyone else under any circumstances. I think that is a major problem for her and for the party. Otherwise, the party might have tried to find a way to survive.”

Jon F Danilowicz, a retired United States diplomat who once served as deputy chief of mission at the US embassy in Dhaka, was more categorical.

“There is zero chance that Hasina will return to Bangladesh in December. In my view, this has all been a bluff intended to rally her supporters and shift the narrative regarding her increasing irrelevance at home,” he told Al Jazeera.

Faiz Sobhan, senior research director at the Bangladesh Enterprise Institute research centre, also sees Hasina’s promise as an effort to lift the morale of her party, which is now banned, with many of its leaders in jail or in exile.

“The announcement keeps Sheikh Hasina politically relevant and lets her gauge the mood at home,” he said. “An actual return seems inconceivable, since it would mean facing the gallows or spending the rest of her life behind bars.”

Despite analysts casting doubt on the prospect of Hasina’s return, her announcement appears to have energised some Awami League leaders and supporters.

“Our leader will return. They have tried to stop her before, but they could not stop her. They are conspiring against her again, but she will overcome these conspiracies and return,” an organising secretary of the party’s central executive committee told Al Jazeera, speaking on condition of anonymity from exile in India.

When asked how Hasina would return and what steps the party was taking to facilitate it, many Awami League leaders and supporters said they had no clear idea about her game plan.

“But she has announced that she will return, and I believe she will come back in December, no matter what,” Arman Rahman, a Dhaka-based Awami League activist and former leader of its student wing, told Al Jazeera.

Hasina’s future is also tied to India’s calculations.

New Delhi, her close ally for decades, has sheltered her since she fled Dhaka in August 2024. But her continued presence has become a point of contention between the two countries.

Dhaka has repeatedly sought Hasina’s extradition under a bilateral treaty. New Delhi says it has been examining the requests, with India’s foreign ministry in April saying it wants to “engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties”.

Meanwhile, both countries have signalled an interest in repairing strained ties.

Sreeradha Datta, professor of international affairs at O P Jindal Global University near New Delhi, told Al Jazeera that India regards Hasina as a longstanding friend, even as it tries to separate her presence in the country from its diplomatic engagement with Dhaka.

“Sheikh Hasina is a very good friend of India. [New] Delhi looks at her as a friend whom it will always support. That is our official position,” she said.

Former US diplomat Danilowicz believes New Delhi is increasingly aware of the diplomatic cost of continuing to host Hasina, but is “unlikely to facilitate” her return to Bangladesh.

“While there may be some in India who still believe that Hasina and her party provide them leverage, by now the [Narendra] Modi government must understand the damage that her continued presence in New Delhi is doing to efforts to normalise relations with Bangladesh,” he said.

“I am certain the Modi government would love to see the Hasina problem go away, including by having her find a third country to reside.”

Rahman, of the Centre for Governance Studies, offered a different explanation for why India may continue to shelter Hasina despite the diplomatic complications.

“I think India is finding it difficult to digest her presence, but at the same time, it cannot let her go either,” he said.

“If India does not take responsibility for protecting her now, its other allies in South Asia and elsewhere may lose trust in New Delhi. They may feel that India does not ultimately protect those who have stood by it.”

Rahman believes India may continue to offer Hasina refuge, but is unlikely to help restore her political domain in Bangladesh.

“I don’t think India will abandon her. But at the same time, I don’t think it will provide her with all forms of political protection, particularly by helping her return to Bangladesh and reestablish herself here,” he said.

Datta, meanwhile, does not expect imminent improvement in relations between the neighbours. “I don’t think Bangladesh-India relations will return to normalisation very soon,” he said.

Many are also asking if Hasina could enter into some kind of a political understanding with the governing Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), now controlled by Prime Minister Rahman, son of Hasina’s longtime rival, Khaleda Zia, who passed away a year ago. Rahman himself lived in exile in London when Hasina was in power.

But analysts see little possibility of such a deal, with the Bangladesh Enterprise Institute’s Sobhan describing the idea as a “non-starter”.

“The BNP has little to gain and much to lose from any accommodation with the Awami League. Its base spent 16-plus years being jailed, harassed and sidelined [by Hasina], and any hint of a deal would be seen as a betrayal,” he told Al Jazeera.

On Monday, BNP acting secretary general and Prime Minister Rahman’s political adviser, Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, also dismissed the prospect of Hasina’s return.

“She is deluding herself if she thinks she can return, reimpose fascism and reclaim her throne,” Rizvi said at an event in Dhaka.

Sobhan said the BNP government had little room to act outside the verdict delivered by the International Crimes Tribunal.

“A broader settlement to stabilise the country is hard to imagine, and reconciliation without accountability or an apology is harder still,” he said.

Extradition was the “only formal route” available to Dhaka, Sobhan added. “And it means being dragged back [to Bangladesh], not choosing to return.”

news.originalContent:
US lawmakers call for tighter restrictions on chip sales amid inquiry into Nvidia CEO’s relationship with alleged spy.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s intimate relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy has highlighted divisions in Washington over the export of advanced chips to China.

Huang, the head of one of the most critical firms in the global artificial intelligence race, has long been among Silicon Valley’s most powerful voices arguing against restrictions on high-end chip sales.

For years, the tech executive lobbied United States President Donald Trump to loosen export controls, finding allies in sympathetic administration figures such as David Sacks, Trump’s former AI tsar.

Whereas hawkish voices argued that Beijing should not have access to cutting-edge US technology on national security grounds, Huang and like-minded executives argued that China already had the computing power to make strides in AI and that wider uptake of US technology would help maintain its dominance in the field.

Jensen Huang’s lobbying now faces intense scrutiny following claims that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang — with whom he had an affair — was an intelligence agent recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied the allegations, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

Alice Huang has not publicly commented on the claims, which The New York Times and the Financial Times first reported, citing unnamed US intelligence officials.

Nvidia’s board of directors on Sunday launched an inquiry into Jensen Huang’s relationship, pledging to examine “all available information” while also expressing confidence in the CEO.

Jensen Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, has pledged to cooperate fully with the inquiry and expressed his commitment to protecting Nvidia and US national security.

Trump has meanwhile said the FBI too is investigating whether Huang’s affair led to any compromise on US national security.

Already, US lawmakers have invoked the controversy to push for tighter restrictions on China’s access to US chips.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren and Republican Senator Jim Banks on Monday called on the US Congress to take “decisive action” and pass their AI Overwatch Act, which would empower lawmakers to scrutinise and potentially halt exports of advanced chips to China and other adversaries.

“The Commerce Department should complement these efforts with immediate action to close export control loopholes and ensure that advanced AI chips are not going to China’s military,” Warren and Banks said in a joint statement.

Democratic House Representative Bill Foster also cited Jensen Huang’s relationship in a statement on Monday in which he called on his fellow lawmakers to get his Chip Security Act “across the finish line”.

The legislation, cosponsored by Republican House Representative Bill Huizenga, aims to prevent illicit smuggling to countries such as China by implementing measures to track the location of chips sent overseas.

Advocates of tighter restrictions now have a “much stronger political argument” and are likely to make use of it, said Rui Ma, a tech industry consultant and founder of Tech Buzz China.

“Chip exports to China have been deeply divisive in Washington, and Huang has been one of the strongest advocates for keeping that market open,” Ma told Al Jazeera.

“If his influence is diminished by this investigation, regardless of its eventual findings, those pushing for tighter restrictions will be in a much stronger position,” she said.

Trump, who has forged a close relationship with Jensen Huang since returning to the White House, has taken several actions to make it easier for chip makers to do business with China, while also maintaining significant export controls.

In May last year, the US Department of Commerce announced that it would scrap the previous Biden administration’s “AI Diffusion Rule”, which would have imposed caps on chip exports to more than 100 countries, including some US allies.

In December, Trump said he had granted Nvidia approval to sell its second-most powerful chip, the H200, to China under an arrangement that would see 25 percent of sales paid to the US government.

Nvidia, which controls an estimated 80 to 90 percent of the market for graphics processing units (GPUs) used to run frontier AI, welcomed the decision at the time, saying it would “support high-paying jobs and manufacturing in America”.

On the other hand, Trump has resisted calls to allow exports of Nvidia’s top-of-the-line Blackwell chips, which deliver about 2.5 times the performance of the H200.

“I think recent events likely increase attention on export control loopholes, and add momentum to bills already being discussed in Congress, like the Chip Security Act,” Erich Grunewald, a senior researcher at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, a Washington, DC-based think tank, told Al Jazeera.

While export controls have spurred contentious debate, their effectiveness has been called into question amid China’s steady advances in AI development.

Authorities and analysts have documented widespread smuggling of restricted chips into China, mainly through Southeast Asia.

Chips with compute power equivalent to 1.6 million Nvidia H100s made their way to China in violation of export restrictions up to the end of 2025, according to an estimate by Epoch AI.

Chinese companies have also been able to bypass US law by remotely accessing compute capacity supplied by Nvidia-powered data centres in countries such as Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand.

Gabriel Wildau, managing director at global business advisory firm Teneo, said claims that Huang had been ensnared in an espionage campaign deserved to be treated with skepticism given the anonymous leaks and motives to discredit him and his company.

“President Trump shows no sign that he intends to disrupt the current US-China rapprochement, but he may face new pressure from Congress and hawkish voices inside his administration to address the remote access issue,” Wildau, who focuses on political risk analysis in China, told Al Jazeera.

Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping have already met twice this year: The US president visited Beijing in May, and the Chinese leader reciprocated with a state visit to Washington in September. They are scheduled to meet again next week when Trump visits Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. And they are expected to meet a fourth time in 2026 in December, when Trump hosts the G20 summit in Miami.

“The risk is that Washington acts to close this loophole [in the aftermath of the Huang controversy], and Beijing regards the action as a violation of the bilateral truce,” Wildau said, referring to the trade truce Trump struck with Xi during their summit in South Korea last year.

Chris Clague, an associate fellow at the International Institute for Strategic Studies in London, said the revelations about Jensen Huang would inevitably undermine the “legitimate” argument in favour of allowing tech transfers between the US and China.

“This has made it a little bit easier for his detractors to poke holes in that,” Clague told Al Jazeera. “It’s indicative of the tensions that exist between the US and China, which are never going away, but it shouldn’t derail efforts at finding some sort of compromise.”
news.content: قانون‌گذاران آمریکایی خواستار محدودیت‌های شدیدتر برای فروش تراشه‌ها در بحبوحه تحقیق در مورد رابطه مدیرعامل انویدیا با متهم جاسوسی شدند. رابطه صمیمانه جنسن هوانگ، مدیرعامل انویدیا با زنی که متهم به جاسوسی چینی است، اختلافات واشنگتن را بر سر صادرات تراشه‌های پیشرفته به چین برجسته کرده است. هوانگ، رئیس یکی از حیاتی‌ترین شرکت‌ها در رقابت جهانی هوش مصنوعی، مدت‌هاست که یکی از قدرتمندترین صداهای سیلیکون ولی است که علیه محدودیت‌های فروش تراشه‌های گران‌قیمت بحث می‌کند. سال‌ها، مدیر اجرایی فناوری، رئیس‌جمهور ایالات متحده، دونالد ترامپ را لابی کرد تا کنترل صادرات را کاهش دهد و متحدانی را در چهره‌های دلسوز دولت مانند دیوید ساکس، رئیس سابق ترامپ پیدا کند. در حالی که صداهای جنگ طلب استدلال می کردند که پکن به دلایل امنیت ملی نباید به فناوری پیشرفته ایالات متحده دسترسی داشته باشد، هوانگ و مدیران همفکر استدلال کردند که چین قبلاً قدرت محاسباتی برای پیشرفت در هوش مصنوعی را دارد و استفاده گسترده تر از فناوری ایالات متحده به حفظ سلطه این کشور در این زمینه کمک می کند. لابی جنسن هوانگ اکنون پس از ادعاهایی مبنی بر اینکه آلیس هوانگ، مدیر سابق Megaspeed - که با او رابطه نامشروع داشت - یک مامور اطلاعاتی است که توسط وزارت امنیت دولتی چین استخدام شده بود، با بررسی شدید روبرو است. آلیس هوانگ علناً در مورد این ادعاها اظهار نظر نکرده است، که نیویورک تایمز و فایننشال تایمز به آن اشاره کردند.
